Boundary integrals: comparing that energy with the standard energy of the system isolates the boundary integral of the square of the free surface, which is the quantity to be estimated (proof lines 1494-1507).

Rellich type identity: the boundary condition and Green's identity rewrite the remaining boundary integral as a volume integral over the lower half space, whose integrand is controlled by the source terms through the third equation of the system (proof lines 1509-1530).

Conclusion: integrating the identity of the second step and inserting the volume bound gives the estimate, the factor linear in time coming from the energy terms evaluated at the final time and at the initial time (proof lines 1531-1538).
proof_roadmap: Diagonalise the boundary matrix and introduce the characteristic fields, isolate the boundary integral of the free surface by comparing with the standard energy, apply the boundary condition and Green's identity for a Rellich type identity, and integrate to obtain the estimate (proof lines 1479-1539).

standard_prerequisites.use: Guarantees that the compensated energy is equivalent to the natural energy and that the weight appearing in the exponential factor is bounded.

core_obligations: Expose the mechanism with vanishing interior sources: with the interior source terms set to zero the boundary condition rewrites the boundary integral of the dissipation identity as minus the time derivative of the inner kinetic energy, and a conservation law for a modified inner density with an explicit source is derived and integrated, which shows that the boundary term is non-positive up to data and lower order terms (proof lines 1258-1293).

Restore the sources by matching the boundary data: a smooth extension operator produces a function on the exterior domain which agrees on the boundary with the difference of the two interior data and whose derivatives are controlled by the interior data, and the boundary condition is rewritten with it (proof lines 1294-1312).

Compensate both conservation laws: adding the lower order terms created by the extension to the exterior and the interior conservation laws makes their boundary contributions cancel through the two boundary conditions, leaving a single identity for the derivative of the sum of the two energies (proof lines 1313-1345).

Define the compensated energy: the energy is the sum of the two densities plus the correction terms multiplied by a large constant chosen so that the compensated energy is equivalent to the natural energy, which the assumption makes possible (proof lines 1346-1356).

Absorb the growth: after multiplying by the exponential of a weight built from the norm of the data, the term proportional to that norm is absorbed into the left hand side and the square root term is split with an epsilon inequality, which yields the estimate with the exponential factor (proof lines 1357-1399).
Bound the weight: the assumption bounds the weight by the constant appearing in the statement, which together with the bounds on the extension gives the estimate as stated (proof lines 1400-1403).
proof_roadmap: First run the argument with vanishing interior sources to exhibit the weak dissipativity of the boundary terms, then restore the sources with an extension matching the boundary data, compensate the two conservation laws so that the boundary contributions cancel, define the compensated energy, absorb the growth with an exponential weight and bound that weight by the assumption (proof lines 1258-1404).
task.difficulty_reason: The proposition states that any regular solution of the linearized problem satisfies an energy estimate in which the value at time t is controlled by the initial energy, the square of the time integral of the data norms and the time integral of the product of two data norms, with the exponential of a constant times the size of the data (statement lines 1223-1237). The counted proof runs 147 lines and is a genuine multi stage argument carried out in the span: it first sets the interior sources to zero to exhibit the mechanism, in which the boundary term of the dissipation identity becomes minus the derivative of the inner kinetic energy and a modified conservation law makes that boundary term non-positive up to data, then restores the sources by constructing an extension of the jump of the interior data through a smooth extension operator, adds the resulting lower order terms to both conservation laws so that their boundary contributions cancel, defines a compensated energy equivalent to the natural energy, absorbs the growth term after multiplying by the exponential of a weight, splits the square root term with an epsilon inequality, and finally bounds the weight by the assumption (proof lines 1258-1403). It is recorded as H3 rather than H2 because the estimate is obtained through a multi stage chain (reduction, extension, compensation, absorption, weight control) rather than through one displayed computation, and the span contains no citation command.

General case, by subtracting a matched function: the trace theorem puts the initial value and its time derivative in the two trace spaces, a function on the whole space matching both traces exists with controlled norm, and the first case applied to the difference yields the estimate (proof lines 3369-3385).
proof_roadmap: Reduce by an extension operator to the whole space, treat vanishing initial data by extending across the initial time and applying the Sobolev embedding, and subtract a function matching both traces in the general case (proof lines 3356-3386).
